clue.text: " Young Adam ——, he that shot so trim " (R and J)

definitions.text: Young Adam ——, he that shot so trim " (R and J)

parts.words: Young Adam ——, he that shot so trim " (R and J)
parts.note: a line from Romeo and Juliet with a gap: Mercutio names the archer god of love after the words Young Adam

explanation.surface: A Shakespeare quotation with a name left out for the solver to supply.
explanation.walkthrough: In Romeo and Juliet Mercutio speaks of the love god as 'Young Adam Cupid', alluding to Adam Bell, a famous archer of ballads; the clue blanks out the name.
explanation.definitionFit: The Roman god of love is the archer whose arrows make people fall in love, the one who shot so trim.

clue.text: Follow Tory example-a writer enjoys it

parts.note: to copy is to follow someone's lead
the Tories are the party of the political Right

explanation.surface: An author takes pleasure in imitating a Conservative politician.
explanation.walkthrough: 'example' rounds off the surface: following a Tory example is copying the Right.
explanation.definitionFit: Authors hold the exclusive legal entitlement to reproduce and sell their own work.

clue.text: Dog consumes nothing for tea

indicators.note: the dog eats the nothing, taking it inside itself

parts.note: a peke is a Pekingese dog
O is zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A dog eats nothing at teatime.
explanation.definitionFit: Pekoe is a high-grade black tea made from young leaves.

clue.text: Lack of confidence in Plutonian creed

parts.note: Dis is another name for Pluto, Roman god of the underworld
a creed is a belief

explanation.surface: Doubts about the religion of the underworld.
explanation.walkthrough: Dis is the Roman underworld god Pluto, so 'Plutonian' gives DIS.
explanation.definitionFit: Disbelief is the inability or refusal to accept that something is true, a lack of trust.

clue.text: Palsied old writer ?

parts.note: writer's cramp was once called a palsy named after the professional copyists who suffered it, so a palsied old writer is one of those clerks

explanation.surface: A doddering elderly author whose hands shake.
explanation.walkthrough: The trade name lives on in 'scrivener's palsy', the old term for writer's cramp, which is what makes this professional copyist palsied.
explanation.definitionFit: A professional copyist or clerk of former times who wrote out documents by hand was a scrivener.

clue.text: Possibly he arms about a thousand, or pretends to

definitions.note: a verb phrase standing for a noun: the clue's he is one who pretends

indicators.note: the shuffled letters go around the thousand, sitting on either side of it
possibly signals the letters of he arms may be arranged another way

parts.note: M is the Roman numeral for a thousand

explanation.surface: Perhaps a man takes up roughly a thousand weapons, or only pretends to.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Possibly' rearranges HE ARMS to SHAMER, and 'about' puts it around M; the 'he' of the clue does duty as the definition's subject.
explanation.definitionFit: A shammer is one who feigns or fakes, putting on a false show.

clue.text: But, given the first one, one might yet accept

definitions.text: But, given the first one, one might yet accept

parts.words: But, given the first one, one might yet accept
parts.note: being offered first option on a deal lets you choose to take it, though the word itself means saying no

explanation.surface: Someone may still say yes after a first rejection.
explanation.walkthrough: The commercial phrase 'first refusal' means the right to accept an offer before anyone else, so given it you might accept.
explanation.definitionFit: A refusal is a turning down, yet having first refusal means you get the first chance to say yes.

clue.text: Desirability of a student, in Pierre's view

indicators.note: the a and the student are put inside the French word, as the clue sets them in it

parts.note: vue is the French for view, Pierre standing for any Frenchman
L is a learner, as on a learner driver's plate

explanation.surface: A Frenchman's opinion of how desirable a student is.
explanation.walkthrough: A Frenchman's 'view' is VUE; A and L (learner) go inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Value is the worth or usefulness of something, how much it is wanted or prized.

clue.text: Native of Europe wearing no make-up

indicators.note: make-up read as making up again: the letters of wearing no are put together in a new form

explanation.surface: A European who goes without cosmetics.
explanation.walkthrough: 'make-up' looks like cosmetics but signals the anagram of WEARING NO.
explanation.definitionFit: A Norwegian is a person from Norway, a country of northern Europe.

clue.text: Haggard equestrian

definitions.meaning: H. ... Haggard was the author of King Solomon's Mines

explanation.surface: A gaunt-looking horseman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Haggard' looks like an adjective but is the novelist Henry Rider Haggard.
explanation.definitionFit: A horseback traveller is a rider, and the novelist Haggard's middle name was the same word.

clue.text: A supporter of weaponry. That's plain

definitions.meaning: the wooden shaft that carries the head of an old infantry spear
from the idiom 'as plain as a ...', meaning perfectly obvious

explanation.surface: Someone backing the arms trade, and stating the obvious.
explanation.definitionFit: The shaft of a pike holds up the weapon, and the idiom 'plain as a pikestaff' makes the word stand for obviousness.

clue.text: Misruled, as Hawk recalled

definitions.meaning: led astray or enticed, wrongly guided
falconers call a hawk back by swinging a feathered decoy on a cord

explanation.surface: Badly governed, as some politician named Hawk remembered.
explanation.definitionFit: Enticed into error, and in falconry a hawk recalled with a decoy has been brought back that way.

clue.text: The beak, or the whole bird

definitions.meaning: beak is slang for a magistrate; a local magistrate or official in old England
the female of the ruff, a wading bird; a ruff is also a collar, so the female is the whole bird rather than a frill

explanation.surface: Choosing between just the bill of a bird and all of it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Beak' is British slang for a magistrate. The ruff is both a collar and a wading bird; its female has its own name.
explanation.definitionFit: An old English shire official or magistrate, and the female ruff, a sandpiper, share the same name.

clue.text: A ram is, in a word, such as he

definitions.text: A ram is, in a word, such as he

parts.words: A ram is, in a word, such as he
parts.note: join the words a ram is into one word and you get Aramis, one of Dumas's three swordsmen in the French king's guard

explanation.surface: A male sheep described as typical of some man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In a word' tells you to run 'A ram is' together: Aramis, one of Dumas's Three Musketeers.
explanation.definitionFit: Aramis is one of the king's guardsmen in Dumas's novel, so he is such a soldier.

clue.text: He may take pains, we hear, to effect a frame-up

definitions.text: He may take pains, we hear, to effect a frame-up

parts.words: He may take pains, we hear, to effect a frame-up
parts.note: pains sounds like panes of window glass, and a frame-up is fitting glass into a frame rather than framing someone

explanation.surface: A careful conspirator working hard to frame an innocent person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pains, we hear' gives panes; 'frame-up' looks like a false accusation but means putting glass into a window frame.
explanation.definitionFit: A tradesman who cuts and fits window glass into frames is a glazier.

clue.text: He recovered his brother's wife from Paris

definitions.text: He recovered his brother's wife from Paris

parts.words: He recovered his brother's wife from Paris
parts.note: Paris is the Trojan prince who carried off Helen, not the French capital; the king of Mycenae led the Greeks to win her back for Menelaus

explanation.surface: A man brought his sister-in-law home from a trip to France.
explanation.walkthrough: Paris is the Trojan who abducted Helen, wife of Menelaus; his brother led the Greek army that took her back.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek legend the leader of the Greek expedition against Troy was Menelaus's brother, king of Mycenae.

clue.text: A long time in regular regiments, like the Lions

indicators.note: the long time is set inside the regiments, as the clue says it is in them

parts.note: line regiments are the regular infantry regiments of the army, called the line
an aeon or eon is an immensely long period

explanation.surface: Ages served in the regular army, with soldiers as brave as lions.
explanation.walkthrough: The British army's regular infantry regiments are known collectively as 'the line', hence line regiments; 'A long time' is a single phrase for an aeon, not A plus another piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Leonine is an adjective meaning resembling or characteristic of the big cats of that name.

clue.text: No universal release mechanism for a light vessel

parts.note: O is zero, none
U is the film certificate for universal viewing
a trigger releases the hammer of a gun

explanation.surface: No standard device for letting go is available for a small boat.
explanation.walkthrough: U is the British film rating for universal audiences.
explanation.definitionFit: A light canoe with a float on a projecting frame for stability is called by the name of that frame.

clue.text: Such the fretful powers Lear contended with

definitions.text: Such the fretful powers Lear contended with

parts.words: Such the fretful powers Lear contended with
parts.note: in King Lear the old king rages on the heath in the storm, contending with the fretful elements, the forces of nature

explanation.surface: A description of the storm King Lear struggled against.
explanation.walkthrough: In King Lear a gentleman reports the king 'contending with the fretful elements'.
explanation.definitionFit: Elemental means of the forces of nature such as wind and storm, the elements Lear battled.

clue.text: Jam-maker's trade?

parts.note: the jam is not preserves but a road jam, made by vehicles; the word for vehicles on roads also means commerce

explanation.surface: Asking what a preserves manufacturer's line of business is.
explanation.walkthrough: What makes a traffic jam is traffic, and traffic also means trade, as in 'traffic in goods'.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both vehicles moving on roads, which cause jams, and commercial dealing in goods.

clue.text: Crimson vehicle belonging to me

parts.note: a car is a vehicle
mine means belonging to me

explanation.surface: My red car.
explanation.definitionFit: Carmine is a vivid crimson colour from cochineal.

clue.text: Train attendants

definitions.meaning: a train is the body of followers accompanying a great person
the people who wait on someone important

explanation.surface: Staff who work on the railway.
explanation.definitionFit: A retinue is the group of followers or servants accompanying an important person, also called a train.

clue.text: Summary many continued after a break

parts.note: a résumé is a summary
D is the Roman numeral 500, taken as many

explanation.surface: A summary of many things carried on after an interruption.
explanation.walkthrough: D as Roman 500 stands for 'many'.
explanation.definitionFit: To resume is to begin again after a pause, so resumed means carried on after stopping.

clue.text: Treasure-store he's found in The Bull

indicators.note: the words he's are located inside the bull, so they are put inside it

parts.note: Taurus is the zodiac sign and constellation of the Bull
taken as its letters, HES

explanation.surface: A man has discovered a hoard of riches inside a pub called The Bull.
explanation.walkthrough: Taurus, the Bull of the zodiac, has HES put inside it after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek source word meant treasury or storehouse, and a book of synonyms is a storehouse of words.

clue.text: Small child gets me up this pole

parts.note: a tot is a small child

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the word me is read from bottom to top

explanation.surface: A little child gets me to climb this pole.
explanation.walkthrough: 'this pole' points at a totem pole, a carved post. In a down clue 'up' reverses ME.
explanation.definitionFit: A totem is the carved emblem on a tribal post, the carved pole of Pacific Northwest peoples.

clue.text: A jester turned up on one side

indicators.note: in a down clue turned up means the jester's word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: a fool is a court jester

explanation.surface: A clown arrives standing apart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned up' reverses FOOL in this down clue, giving LOOF.
explanation.definitionFit: Aloof means apart, distant, standing off to one side.

clue.text: Outlet for children

definitions.meaning: a way out, where something flows forth

explanation.surface: A place for kids to go, or a way of letting off steam.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means a point of outflow and also a person's offspring or descendants.

clue.text: Showing, unnatural keenness

parts.note: in music a note raised a semitone is not natural; the sign that shows this also means keen or acute

explanation.surface: Displaying an odd eagerness.
explanation.walkthrough: In written music a note is either natural or raised by a sign; the same word means keen-edged.
explanation.definitionFit: A musical sign raises a note from natural pitch, and the same word describes a keen blade or wit.

clue.text: Steps into a tartan gown ?

indicators.note: the answer runs into and across the words tartan gown, sitting inside them

explanation.surface: Someone walks into a Scottish plaid dress.
explanation.walkthrough: Hidden in tarTAN GOwn; 'Steps' is the definition, a dance's steps.
explanation.definitionFit: A tango is a ballroom dance, a sequence of steps, from Argentina.

clue.text: I'm having a motorway allowance, being a settler

parts.note: taken as its letters, IM
motorway gives MI
a grant is an allowance of money

explanation.surface: Someone settling in a new country gets a payment for using the motorway.
explanation.walkthrough: British motorways are named M1, M6 and so on, so M is motorway.
explanation.definitionFit: An immigrant comes from abroad to live permanently in a new country, settling there.

clue.text: No overhead charges here

parts.note: the charges are explosive ones buried underground, not business overheads, so none are above the ground

explanation.surface: A place of business with no running costs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Overhead charges' suggests business costs, but these charges are explosives, all laid below ground.
explanation.definitionFit: An area where explosive mines are buried beneath the surface is a minefield.

clue.text: Drive back quietly in the middle of the dance

indicators.note: the quiet letter is placed in the centre of the dance

parts.note: a reel is a lively Scottish or Irish dance
p is the musical abbreviation for piano, softly

explanation.surface: Retreating while softly dancing.
explanation.walkthrough: P (piano, quietly in music) goes into REEL.
explanation.definitionFit: To repel an attack is to force it back, to drive the attackers away.
